[1] Collaboration.md (Auto-merging concurrent edits)
  - A genuine binary conflict in SilverBullet produces a sibling copy named name.conflicted-<hash>.ext next to the original, where <hash> is a short hash of the losing version's bytes.
  Binary conflicts: Images, PDFs and other binaries (and text files over the 1 MB merge limit) can’t be merged, so a genuine conflict instead produces a sibling copy named `name.conflicted-<hash>.ext` next to the original, where `<hash>` is a short hash of the losing version’s bytes.
  - When both sides really changed the same words, SilverBullet writes the file with Git-style conflict markers.
  - A reference page explaining how SilverBullet merges concurrent edits to the same file, how conflicts are written and shown, and how live external, offline and deletion cases are handled. Names: SilverBullet, Google Docs, Desktop, Git, Obsidian.
  - The SilverBullet editor Live Previews each conflicted section as an edit conflict widget showing both sides as well as the original.
[2] Guide/Make it your own.md (Get comfortable)
  - If SilverBullet reports a shortcut conflict, another key combination must be chosen.
[3] Install/Docker.md (Release channels)
  Release channels: Every release version of SilverBullet is tagged with its version number, but there are two release channels you can use: / * `:latest` always points to the latest _release_. / * `:edge` always points to the latest _edge build_ (the last commit to `main`). / The default image includes Chromium and enables the [[Runtime API]]. For the smaller image without Chromium, use `:edge-slim` instead of `:edge` or legacy `:v2`, `:latest-slim` instead of `:latest`, or append `-slim` to a version such as `:2.11.0-slim`.
